summary: This PHP script handles CSV-to-Markdown conversion. When it receives a POST request with CSV data and formatting options, it processes them using a Csv2Md class and returns the markdown result. Otherwise, it displays an HTML form with a Vue.js interface that lets users paste CSV data, adjust delimiters and formatting, and see the conversion result live.

explanations.3: This tells PHP to enforce strict type checking, meaning function parameters and return types must match their declared types exactly.
explanations.26: This reads the raw JSON data sent by the frontend, converts it from JSON format into a PHP array, and stores it in $data.
explanations.29: This extracts the 'task' value from the data array, sanitizes it to remove any HTML/special characters, and uses an empty string if 'task' wasn't provided.
explanations.33: The CSV content is base64-encoded when sent from the frontend (for safe transmission), so we decode it back to plain text here.
explanations.36: Similar to line 33, we decode the delimiter which was base64-encoded, then check if it's empty and default to a comma if it is.
explanations.56: This converts the 'transpose' value (which arrives as a string like 'true' or 'false') into an actual boolean true/false that PHP can use.
explanations.59: We create a new instance of the Csv2Md class, which is a custom parser object that will handle the actual conversion work.
explanations.68: We set the HTTP response header to 'text/plain' so the browser knows it's receiving plain text, not HTML.
explanations.69: We encode the markdown result back into base64 for safe transmission to the frontend, then send it back.
explanations.76: This checks if a template file named 'octocat.tmpl' exists in the current directory, storing the file path in $cat only if it does.
explanations.77: We read the contents of the template file, replace a placeholder '%REPO%' with the actual GitHub repository URL, and store the result.
explanations.188: The btoa() function is JavaScript's way to base64-encode data, so we're encoding the CSV content before sending it to the server.
explanations.195: The atob() function decodes the base64 response from the server back into plain text, which we then store in the Markdown variable.
explanations.203: We grab the plain text from what the user pasted, rather than letting Vue use its default behavior.
explanations.204: This regex finds all tab characters (the whitespace character) and replaces them with commas, making pasted Excel data compatible.
explanations.215: The marked() function converts our Markdown table syntax into HTML table tags that can be displayed in a browser.
